questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Decorator pattern?

options.text: Attach additional responsibilities to an object dynamically, as a flexible alternative to subclassing
Convert one interface into another
Compose objects into tree structures
Provide a simplified interface to a subsystem

questions.explanation: Decorator adds behavior dynamically while keeping the same interface. Converting interfaces = Adapter; trees = Composite; simplifying = Facade.

questions.prompt: What does a decorator keep the same as the object it wraps?

options.text: Its interface, so clients can't tell it's wrapped
Its exact memory address
Nothing — it changes the interface
Its private constructor

questions.explanation: A decorator implements the same Component interface, so it's transparent to callers and can be stacked.

questions.prompt: How does Decorator differ from Proxy?

options.text: Both keep the same interface, but Decorator adds behavior while Proxy controls access
Decorator changes the interface; Proxy keeps it
They are the same pattern
Proxy adds behavior; Decorator clones the object

questions.explanation: Decorator and Proxy both wrap with the same interface; the difference is intent — adding responsibilities vs controlling access.

questions.prompt: What common bug breaks a decorator chain?

options.text: Overriding a method but forgetting to forward the call to the wrapped object
Using an interface
Making the base component immutable
Injecting the component

questions.explanation: Decorators must delegate calls they don't specifically change; forgetting to forward makes the wrapped behavior vanish.

questions.prompt: How is the GoF Decorator pattern different from TypeScript's @decorator language feature?

options.text: The GoF Decorator is a wrapping design pattern; @decorator is a language feature for annotating classes/members
They are identical
The GoF Decorator only works with the @ syntax
@decorator can only create singletons

questions.explanation: Same name, different mechanism: one is a runtime object-wrapping pattern, the other is annotation syntax.

questions.prompt: Which are advantages of Decorator over subclassing every combination? Select all that apply.

options.text: Behaviors can be combined at runtime in any order
It avoids a class explosion of feature combinations
Each decorator can stay small and single-purpose
It guarantees only one instance of the object

questions.explanation: Decorator gives runtime combination, avoids the combinatorial subclass explosion, and keeps each wrapper focused. Single-instance is Singleton.
